what_it_does: Modern processors speed things up by guessing ahead — executing future instructions before they are officially needed (called speculative execution). Attacks like Spectre exploit this by tricking the processor into speculatively reading secret data and leaving traces in the CPU's internal state (for example in the cache) that an attacker can then measure. SpecASan defends against this by extending ARM's memory-tagging feature — a mechanism that attaches a small color-code to every pointer and memory region to catch bugs — from normal committed execution into the speculative phase. If a speculative memory read uses a pointer whose color does not match the target memory's color, the access is paused until speculation resolves, preventing any secret information from leaking into observable hardware state. The approach reuses existing tagging hardware and requires very little new silicon. Details are from the abstract only.
